predecessors.name: Tenson Dynasty
predecessors.text: Okinawa Island, where 'the last overlord of Tenson dynasty was assassinated' by Riyū, whom Shunten overthrew

successors.name: Chūzan
successors.text: central Okinawa around Urasoe, where the Eiso kings Tamagusuku and Seii continued as Chūzan to 1349

successors.name: Hokuzan
successors.text: the north: the lord of Nakijin 'declared himself independent of Chūzan and crowned himself as the King of Hokuzan'

successors.name: Nanzan
successors.text: the south: 'The lord (aji) of Ōzato left for his own castle and declared himself to be King of Nanzan'

ledger.x: 1187: Shunten, lord of Urasoe, recognised as king of Okinawa.
1259: Gihon abdicates to his regent Eiso; the Eiso dynasty.
1314: the Sanzan period; the Eiso kings continue as Chūzan at Urasoe.

wars.name: Shunten's revolt against Riyū
wars.outcome: 'Shunten revolted against Riyū and overthrew him'; 'In 1187, Shunten was recognized as the new king'.

certainty.note: A Gusuku-period chiefdom: no borders on the pages; the extent beyond Urasoe (the whole island, the Kerama and Kume islands, Amami) is unverified.
